reconciliationFindings: The direct packaged result preserves exact artifact identity, exact target selection, all 14 operation/history-binding entries, all 11 history states, bounded preview/approval coverage, explicit later-state gaps, and the read-only/non-certifying/no-execution boundary.

The packaged observation exposes metadata only; it does not prove a transition for any history state, an authoritative project reread, undo/redo, stale or timeout recovery, a committed outcome, or aggregate active-GM/Foundry authority.

The 14-operation surface does not by itself reconcile the eleven producer families or prove that every mutating producer has the required inspectable batch, approval, execution receipt, reread, undo, and recovery behavior.
No project or session was present and no mutation occurred, so the local review/apply/undo live clause remains unproven while the no-write boundary is preserved.
remainingGaps: Cross-producer lifecycle, authoritative reread, undo/redo, stale/timeout recovery, and commit evidence remain distributed across bounded slices.
The existing binding records preview/approval coverage but does not provide a typed state-by-operation lifecycle coverage matrix for the 14 operations and 11 states.
Broader recovery/cleanup remains separately gated and cannot be inferred from packaged metadata visibility.
Technical Builder/repository and active-GM/Foundry authority remain distinct boundaries.
reconciliation.smallestRemainingGap: A typed, read-only, non-certifying operation/history lifecycle coverage matrix derived from the existing 14-operation binding and 11-state vocabulary, showing observed preview/approval coverage and explicit unobserved later-state gaps without executing or adding authority.

decision.reason: M620 preserves the M619 packaged operation-history binding pass, but direct visibility remains non-certifying and read-only. The four Stage 11 clauses still lack contradiction-free cross-producer lifecycle, recovery, commit, reread, and authority evidence.
